what_its_for: Cevimeline is used to treat dry mouth in people who have Sjogren's syndrome, a condition where the immune system attacks the glands that make saliva and tears. This medicine helps your salivary glands produce more saliva so your mouth feels less dry and more comfortable.
how_to_take: Take cevimeline by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Try to drink plenty of fluids throughout the day while taking this medicine to stay hydrated. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is 30 mg (one capsule) taken three times a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well it works for you and any side effects you may have. Do not take more than your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cevimeline at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause blurred vision or difficulty seeing clearly, especially at night. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of water, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Avoid taking this medicine if you have certain eye conditions like narrow-angle glaucoma or if you have uncontrolled asthma, unless your doctor says it is safe. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, as some medicines can interact with cevimeline.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: vision changes or eye pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing or wheezing, severe sweating, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not stop, dizziness or fainting, tremors or shaking, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your dry mouth does not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your dry mouth symptoms within a few weeks of starting cevimeline. It may take up to 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not notice immediate improvement.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of cevimeline, such as dizziness, sweating, and vision changes, so use with caution. This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy unless clearly needed — talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. It is not known if cevimeline passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding mothers should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The safety and effectiveness of cevimeline in children has not been established. People with kidney or liver problems may need a dose adjustment, so make sure your doctor knows your full medical history.
